experience.description: Owned and shipped a facility-data automation tool for HISinOne, from system design and service integration through production verification.

paragraphs: The facility team was entering building and room data into HISinOne by hand from spreadsheets and WebUntis. That made a simple data update slow and left too much room for missing or inconsistent records.

I built the automation end to end: a SOAP/WSDL client for WebUntis, an authenticated HISinOne API client, and a hierarchical resolution pipeline that works through building, floor, and room data independently. Ambiguous matches are flagged instead of guessed, and missing records are detected before they reach production.

The first live run processed 200+ records across 10+ buildings with zero errors. I also added a fully automated pytest suite and independent post-import checks so the result could be verified rather than simply assumed.

experience.description: Built and optimized a real-time logistics dashboard in Angular, while helping move the team from Vue to Angular.

paragraphs: I worked on a logistics tracking dashboard where real-time updates and load performance mattered during active tracking.

I rebuilt the frontend around Angular and RxJS streams, introduced custom lazy-loading, and optimized the GraphQL fragments used by the dashboard. The changes improved real-time synchronization by 25% and reduced initial load time by 40%.

I also reduced server overhead by 30% through debounce strategies and disciplined Angular lifecycle management. Alongside the implementation work, I led the migration of two developers from Vue to Angular, established coding standards, and introduced mentoring practices that reduced code-review cycle time by 15%.
I worked with backend engineers on end-to-end testing to verify that data moved correctly across the frontend and backend before release.

experience.description: Built Eber across the stack, from the Angular application and real-time tracking to the Node.js backend, APIs, payments, and notifications.

paragraphs: I worked on Eber, an on-demand ride-booking platform, and owned features across both the frontend and backend.
On the frontend, I built the Angular 18 application with Google Maps tracking, live ride updates over WebSockets, Stripe payments, and a responsive PWA-enabled interface.

On the backend, I built the Node.js/Express/MongoDB services for the ride lifecycle, including driver assignment, trip completion, dynamic pricing, automated invoice generation, and REST APIs used by the admin panel and planned mobile clients.
I also built multi-channel notifications using Twilio SMS, email, and browser push, plus an admin dashboard with ride history, filtering, CSV export, and live trip-path visualization.

engineeringPrinciples.label: Features
engineeringPrinciples.statement: Start with the problem, not the feature.
engineeringPrinciples.explanation: I try to understand what actually needs to change before deciding what to build. At HFT, that meant automating accurate facility records rather than building another interface around a manual process.

engineeringPrinciples.label: Systems
engineeringPrinciples.statement: Build systems that stay understandable as they grow.
engineeringPrinciples.explanation: I care about clear boundaries, responsibilities, and data flow because they make systems easier to change when the product gets bigger.

engineeringPrinciples.label: Trade-offs
engineeringPrinciples.statement: Every engineering decision moves complexity somewhere.
engineeringPrinciples.explanation: I want the reason behind a technical choice to be understandable, including what it makes easier and what it makes harder later.

engineeringPrinciples.label: Reliability
engineeringPrinciples.statement: If it matters, I want a way to verify it.
engineeringPrinciples.explanation: Tests, validation, failure handling, and post-deployment checks are part of the work, not something added after the feature is finished.

services.title: Full-stack Development
services.description: Build the path from interface to API and database, with testing and deployment included.

paragraphs: I’m comfortable owning a feature across the stack rather than treating frontend and backend as separate worlds.
That means thinking about the data model, API contract, interface, tests, and deployment together so the pieces work as one product.

services.title: Frontend Engineering
services.description: Build React and Angular interfaces that remain responsive under real data and real interaction.

paragraphs: Most frontend problems become interesting when the data is live, the network is slow, or the product has to change without breaking what already works.
My experience with Angular, RxJS, GraphQL, React, and performance work has taught me to treat the interface as part of the system, not just its presentation layer.

services.title: Backend & API Design
services.description: Design Node.js and NestJS services with clear contracts, data flow, and maintainable boundaries.

paragraphs: I think about an API as the boundary between parts of a system. The contract, data model, validation, error handling, and ownership rules all matter.
My backend work spans Node.js, NestJS, Express, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, REST, GraphQL, and service integrations.

services.title: Software Architecture
services.description: Design software around clear boundaries, data flow, and the trade-offs that come with growth.

paragraphs: This is the area I’m developing most deliberately through my M.Sc. in Software Technology.
I’m interested in how systems stay understandable, testable, and reliable as they become more distributed, and I apply that thinking in projects such as SynthGraph and in my production work.

services.title: AI-assisted Engineering
services.description: Use agentic coding tools inside explicit architecture, testing, and review boundaries.

paragraphs: I use AI coding tools to move faster, but I don’t want the tool deciding what the system should become.
The useful part is combining agentic implementation with architecture documents, explicit constraints, tests, and review so speed does not quietly turn into design drift.
